title: controlplane-weekly-huddle-routing-auth-quotas-2026-11-03
content:
Attendees: Asha K (chair), Miles C, Riley O, Samir P, J. Lee, Priya (SRE), Sienna (DS)

Purpose: quick weekly sync focused on current control plane work that spans routing, auth, and quota subsystems. Capture blockers, short-term plans, and cross-team handoffs. This is intentionally informal — notes, rough todos, and follow-ups.

Topline metrics (last 7d):
- Avg route decision latency (p95): 12ms (target 10ms) — slight regression after the allocator change rolled 10/28
- Auth token validation success rate: 99.96% (target 99.99%) — bulk of failures are transient 5xx from KMS integration
- Quota enforcement miss rate: 0.03% (target <0.01%) — correlated with high-concurrency bursts
- Incidents since last sync: 1 (RW-INC-610) — expired caches causing transient over-quota for some Dedicated customers

Round-robin updates

Asha (Control Plane lead)
- Status: focusing on rollout mitigation for allocator/routing change. Deployed a short-term circuit breaker to avoid expensive topological recomputation under bursty traffic. Observed p95 latency drop to 9.8ms for a small cohort (canary) after flip.
- Next: formalize circuit-breaker config as a per-customer routing-policy flag and add tests. Spike for config UI in Console next week.
- Blocker: need API gateway team to cut a small auth header passthrough change, ticketed RW-2148. Waiting on API gateway review.
- Notes-to-self: remind infra to snapshot old allocator state before next major tweak (we lost traces this weekend and it slowed triage).

Miles (Routing)
- Status: routing optimizer v2 on candidate branch. Improved path scoring to include regional cost buckets. Local perf looks good, but integration tests reveal a rare route reshuffle when very short sequence lengths arrive (LLMs short-chat). Hypothesis: scoring normalization bug when token count < 8.
- Action: add unit tests for short-sequence normalization + add a regression test to nightly harness.
- PR: opened PR 542 (link above). Need 1 more reviewer from platform-engineering (volunteer: J. Lee?).

Riley (Auth)
- Status: KMS rekey experiment is in progress. We see ~0.04% additional latency on token validation when KMS cold starts. For high-RPS flows, those cold starts produce 502 spikes that our retry logic turns into brief auth failures.
- Mitigation: SRE suggested a small warmup shim and caching layer for KMS clients (Priya to scope). Riley will instrument cache hit ratio and add telemetry counters.
- Outstanding question: what's the SLO for token validation 99.99% = allowed 43 min/year. We are close — need prioritized fix vs. a longer-term redesign.

Samir (Quotas & Billing)
- Status: investigating quota enforcement miss RW-2141 where a combination of distributed quota shards and lease expiry caused double-consume during leader failover.
- Temporary mitigation: increase lease buffer and tighten leader election jitter. Post-mitigation we saw one fewer miss in the test harness.
- Longer-term: moving to a hybrid token-bucket + write-through cache for dedicated customers to avoid cross-shard race windows.
- Blocker: needs product clarification on whether Dedicated customers expect strict linearizable quota enforcement (product folks: do we treat quotas as strong or eventual for reserved vs hosted?).

Priya (SRE)
- Incident recap: RW-INC-610 — expired cache entries (KV cache TTL mis-set to 0 for a micro-update) caused quota checks to fallback to slower DB path which timed out under burst and returned 503 -> surfaced as over-quota to clients. Fix deployed, still monitoring.
- Follow-ups: add runbook entry for cache TTL misconfig and an automated check that emits alerts when cache miss rate > 0.5% for 5m.
- Note: recommend a prefailure test that artificially drops cache and validates quorum.

Sienna (Data/ML metrics)
- Working on a small eval to measure user-visible regressions from routing changes using 100 synthetic prompts. Early signal: V2 routing reduces latency by avg 8% but yields a small increase in reroute events for cold models. Need to decide acceptable tradeoff.

Cross-cutting decisions
- Short-term: keep circuit-breaker enabled for 2 weeks in canary and 1 week in progressively larger cohorts; collect p95 and error-rate deltas per-customer. Decision owner: Asha (owner).
- Mid-term: add a per-customer routing-policy switch in the Console so support/product can flip back to old allocator if customers see regressions. Scope out prior to Dedicated on-boarding next quarter. (Ticket: CONFLUENCE-CP-ROADMAP-2026)

Open questions / discussion items
- Quotas consistency model: product to decide strictness for Dedicated customers. Samir flagged customer expectations; product input requested by 2026-11-10.
- Auth timeout SLOs: do we accept a short-term SLA hit while implementing KMS warmup? Security to weigh in — security@redwood recommended failing closed is preferable.
- Routing scoring edge-case for short sequences: Miles to propose normalization patch by EOD 11/05.

Action items (owner — eta)
- Miles: add short-seq normalization tests and update PR 542 (11/05)
- J. Lee: review PR 542 and provide feedback (11/06)
- Riley + Priya: prototype KMS warmup shim and add telemetry counters (11/09)
- Samir: draft product question re: quota strictness and send to product-hosted-api + legal (11/10)
- Asha: design console toggle spec for per-customer routing-policy and sync with PM (11/12)
- SRE: add cache-TTL automated check to monitoring runbook (Priya) (11/07)

Misc notes / rough ideas
- Could we leverage our Optimize signals to feed routing decisions (cost thresholds) dynamically? sketch: offline eval -> hot path classification -> live rollout via flags.
- Consider a small internal SLA tier for dedicated beta customers where we guarantee linearizable quotas — premium for early adopters.
- Reminder: backlog cleanup sprint next week; folks add stale tickets with label "cp-triage" so we can close FG issues.

Attachments / links referenced inline
- RW-2148 (API gateway header passthrough) — blocking the per-customer routing flag rollout
- RW-2141 (quota miss investigation)
- RW-INC-610 (cache expiry incident)
- PR 542: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/542
- Roadmap doc: CONFLUENCE-CP-ROADMAP-2026

Closing: quick pulse check — thumbs up to proceeding with canary circuit-breaker expansion. Next huddle: 2026-11-10 09:30 PT. Please add any follow-ups directly to this doc or ping #pltfm-controlplane on Slack if urgent.

Notes to self (Asha): follow up with product on quota strictness, remind infra about allocator snapshots, add checklist for circuit-breaker config review.
